title: Applied AI Engineer
summary: A product-oriented engineer who turns uncertain model capability into useful, measurable, reliable, and governable behavior for defined users and tasks.

includes: Define task-specific product behavior and maintain the evidence loop from hypothesis through operation and controlled change.
Build and evaluate the combined data, model, software, interface, control, and operating system around learned behavior.
Prepare technical evidence, expose limitations, and route product, domain, legal, safety, privacy, security, and formal risk decisions to named authorities.
excludes: Create frontier model capability as a research scientist or own the full model and data platform lifecycle by default.
Own customer engagement delivery, commercial commitments, product-roadmap priority, or every system dependency by default.
Act as legal counsel, domain authority, independent auditor, or unilateral safety, privacy, security, and business risk acceptor.

competencies.title: Task, value, and AI decision
competencies.description: Define a consequential user task and test whether an AI mechanism is justified.

objectives.statement: Define the user task and consequence, test the value hypothesis, and choose AI only when evidence supports it.

competencies.title: Behavior contracts and boundaries
competencies.description: Specify observable behavior, uncertainty, system limits, and escalation paths.

objectives.statement: Specify observable behavior, uncertainty, non-goals, escalation, degradation, and system and authority boundaries.

competencies.title: Model and mechanism selection
competencies.description: Compare learned and deterministic mechanisms against task evidence and constraints.

objectives.statement: Compare deterministic, search, predictive, generative, agentic, adapted, and hybrid mechanisms under real constraints.

competencies.title: Data, context, retrieval, and grounding
competencies.description: Construct authorized, representative task evidence and runtime context paths.

objectives.statement: Build authorized, representative task inputs and context paths with provenance, relevance, leakage, and limitation controls.

competencies.title: Production application and integration
competencies.description: Implement inspectable software and controls around uncertain learned behavior.

objectives.statement: Implement services, schemas, interfaces, orchestration, tools, validation, permissions, and user feedback around learned behavior.

competencies.title: Evaluation and experimentation
competencies.description: Build representative evidence and experiments tied to user consequence.

objectives.statement: Create representative evidence, error taxonomies, segmented judgments, calibrated review, experiments, and release dispositions.

competencies.title: Operational quality and observability
competencies.description: Engineer and diagnose the quality, reliability, latency, capacity, and cost envelope.

objectives.statement: Engineer reliability, latency, throughput, capacity, cost, privacy-safe signals, diagnosis, fallback, and recovery.

competencies.title: Responsible controls and authority
competencies.description: Implement proportionate controls while preserving named decision authority.

objectives.statement: Implement and test proportionate privacy, security, safety, abuse, governance, and human-authority controls without self-authorizing risk.

competencies.title: Release, feedback, and incident learning
competencies.description: Bound exposure and turn production feedback and incidents into verified improvement.

objectives.statement: Bound rollout, monitor use and behavior, respond to incidents, and convert production evidence into controlled improvement.

competencies.title: Change, portability, and evidence-earned reuse
competencies.description: Preserve product behavior through change and standardize only after repeated evidence.

objectives.statement: Survive model, provider, and data change and build reusable mechanisms only when repeated evidence justifies them.

competencies.title: Advanced technical leadership
competencies.description: Set evidence standards and lead cross-system decisions without absorbing adjacent authority.

objectives.statement: Set evidence standards, resolve cross-system tradeoffs, communicate limitations, mentor teams, and preserve adjacent-role authority.
